title: The app shell
summary: Four tabs, a back button that walks back through the app, and a layout that follows the window.
description: One interface for a phone, a tablet and a computer, built from a small design system.

stories.as: a learner using a phone and a computer
stories.want: the same app laid out for each screen
the back button to walk back through the app
stories.soThat: it behaves like every other app on my phone

requirements.text: Exercises is the home screen: today's lessons on top, then the courses.
Android's back button closes a sheet first, then the page, then goes from another tab to Exercises, and leaves the app only from Exercises.
Below `layout.rail-from` of window width the tabs are at the bottom; from `layout.rail-from` they form a rail at the left edge.
From `layout.split-from` a course's or a lesson's page is laid out in two columns, and Settings shows its menu beside the open page.
Search lists every word and sentence in the app, met or not, filterable by course and searchable in Polish or English.
On Android the page lays out above the keyboard, and the tab bar is hidden while typing.
Light and dark themes are both supported; the theme is a setting of the device.
The design system's buttons are `control.md` high by default and `control.sm` in their small size.
Destructive actions use the design system's confirm button, which asks before acting.
The design system has an empty state for lists, which says what would be there and can offer the action that fills it.
The build fails when a screen breaks the design system's mechanical rules.
The brand colour is `color.brand`, the background `color.bg` and body text `color.text`, each with its own value in the dark theme.
A right answer is shown in `color.ok` and a wrong one in `color.bad`.
